title: Crispy Coconut Shrimp with Rice
subtitle: golden coconut-panko shrimp baked crisp, with jasmine rice and a sweet orange dipping sauce
imageAlt: Golden coconut-crusted shrimp with a small bowl of orange dipping sauce and rice on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Flour, oil, lemon juice, soy, salt

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw the shrimp overnight in the fridge. Peel, leaving the tails on, devein and pat very dry.
Oven at 220°C (425°F) with a wire rack set on a rimmed baking sheet, so the bottoms crisp too.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Set up
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Season the shrimp with the salt. Put the flour in one shallow dish, the eggs in another, and the coconut and panko mixed in a third.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Holding each shrimp by the tail, dip it in flour, then egg, then press firmly into the coconut mix. Lay on the rack and drizzle or brush lightly with the oil.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 10–12 minutes, turning once, until golden and the shrimp are pink, opaque and 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Dip
steps.text: Warm the marmalade with the lemon juice and soy sauce in the microwave 30 seconds and stir smooth.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the shrimp with the rice and the dip on the side.

fixIt.fix: Dry the shrimp well and press them firmly into the coconut mix.

fixIt.problem: Coconut too dark before the shrimp are done
fixIt.fix: Move the pan to a lower rack and drop the heat to 200°C (400°F).
Bake on a wire rack, or turn them halfway.

saleTip: Larger 21–25 shrimp are worth it here; watch for the No Frills frozen seafood sale.
swap: Air fryer: 200°C (400°F) 7–8 minutes in one layer, in batches, turning once.
leftovers: Best fresh; re-crisp in the air fryer 3–4 minutes.
doneness: Shrimp 74°C (165°F): pink and opaque all the way through (Health Canada, shellfish).
source: Based on tested baked coconut shrimp methods (Canadian Living, Food Network Canada): flour, egg and coconut-panko coating baked on a rack at 220°C, served with an orange marmalade dip instead of sweet chili sauce.
gear: Rimmed baking sheet with wire rack
prepAhead: Coat the shrimp up to 4 hours ahead; keep them uncovered on the rack in the fridge.
reheat: Air fryer at 190°C (375°F) 3–4 minutes, until 74°C (165°F) and crisp.

basic.note: Panko-coconut shrimp with plain marmalade to dip.

stepNotes.4: Basic: warm the marmalade on its own.

fancy.note: Coconut rice and a squeeze of lime.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: cook the rice in the coconut milk and 1½ cups water instead of 3 cups water.

plating: Rice pressed into a small bowl and turned out.
Shrimp leaning against it, tails up.
Dip and lime wedges on the side.

why.0-4: Sweetened coconut toasts golden and gives the classic sweet crunch.
why.0-5: Panko keeps the coating crisp and stops the coconut from burning too fast.
why.1-0: Marmalade makes an instant sweet-tangy dip with no heat.

funFact: Coconut shrimp became a 1980s restaurant favourite across North America, inspired by Caribbean and Thai flavours.
airFryer: Air-fry the coated shrimp in one layer at 200°C (400°F) for 6–8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden, pink and opaque, 74°C (165°F). Lightly spray or brush the coating with oil first so it browns.
drink: A tropical white like an off-dry Riesling, or pineapple-coconut iced tea.
